newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: YACHTING-Rescued Briton in good spirits after surgery.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-Rescued Briton in good spirits after surgery.

text.p: Rescued British yachtsman Tony Bullimore was reported to be in good spirits on Tuesday after surgery on a finger, while fellow sailor Thierry Dubois began a countrywide journey to thank his Australian saviours.

Bullimore, who will celebrate his 58th birthday on Wednesday, stayed in Perth after Monday's emotional return aboard an Australian navy frigate to receive treatment for injuries to his hands and feet.

He was kept in the St John of God Hospital overnight after surgery to tidy up the little finger of his left hand, part of which was severed in a hatch accident as he clung to life beneath his upturned yacht.

The evening operation followed the excitement of a heroes' welcome for the two solo round-the-world sailors, an official ceremony, media interviews and, for Bullimore, an emotional reunion with his wife Lalel.
A hospital spokeswoman said the operation went well and Bullimore was "laughing and joking" on Tuesday morning before he was discharged.

The Briton, who also suffered frostbite and other exposure injuries, is expected to continue daily treatment in a decompression chamber to increase the flow of oxygen to his hands and feet, speeding their recovery.
His 81-year-old aunt Dinah Twomey, who lives in Perth, said a family celebration was planned for Bullimore's birthday, although details had not been completed.
"It won't be at my place. There's not enough room because there will be more than just the family attending," Twomey told local media.
The two competitors in the Vendee Globe round-the-world race were picked up on Thursday 400 km southwest of the Australian coast after they capsized in rough seas last Sunday.
Bullimore survived for five days beneath his upturned yacht, his fate unknown until rescuers from the Adelaide knocked on the hull.
Dubois, described by doctors as in excellent health, flew on Tuesday to the southern city of Adelaide, base for the Orion aircraft crews who located the two solo yachtsmen.
The 29-year-old Frenchman is due in the capital Canberra on Wednesday morning to review the five-day rescue operation with defence staff and maritime safety officials.
A commercial television station has purchased Australian rights to Bullimore's tale, and a spokesman said further interviews and news items were planned in coming days.
In an interview broadcast on Tuesday night, Bullimore said he had enjoyed a first beer on dry land.
"I have just had a beer, one little small glass of beer, and that was ecstasy," he said.
The rescue of Dubois and Bullimore has sparked enormous interest in Australia and overseas, particularly in Britain.
Several thousand wellwishers waving flags and banners turned out to greet the pair when they reached dry land on Monday, along with more than 150 local and international media.
Meanwhile on Monday in Montreal, Canadian authorities said it was too early to tell whether satellite images captured the boat of missing Canadian sailor Gerry Roufs.
Roufs, also a Vendee competitor, is missing somewhere between New Zealand, South America and Antarctica.
